walkthrough:
Write down the general term in the binomial expansion of $\left(2x + \frac{1}{4x^2}\right)^6$:
$$T_{r+1} = \binom{6}{r}(2x)^{6-r}\left(\frac{1}{4x^2}\right)^r = \binom{6}{r}2^{6-r}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^r x^{6-3r}$$

Set the power of $x$ equal to zero ($6 - 3r = 0 \implies 3r = 6 \implies r = 2$) to isolate the constant term:
$$T_3 = \binom{6}{2}(2x)^4\left(\frac{1}{4x^2}\right)^2 = 15(16x^4)\left(\frac{1}{16x^4}\right) = 15$$

State the term independent of $x$:
$$\text{Term independent of } x = 15$$
